narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "On the Rail"**

Every lead is a printed ticket clipped to a steel rail at a kitchen pass. The page is brushed steel; anything a machine printed or a person wrote sits on bright thermal paper; ink is near-black. A ticket's top stripe ages from green to heat-lamp orange to late red while it waits, and a person claims it by pressing Heard. The world is an operating object, not a landing page: there is no headline beside a dashboard screenshot and no row of feature cards.

The system is plain and hard-edged. Three faces split the work by who is speaking: a condensed industrial sans for anything stamped or posted (headlines, labels, timers, keys), a narrow monospace for anything the printer produced, and a humanist text face for prose a person reads at length. Colour carries almost no decoration; the age colours exist only to say how long a lead has waited.

Scope: the public front page (`web/index.html`, `web/src/front/`) and the signed-in app (`web/app.html`, `web/src/styles/app.css`). Both read every colour, face and spacing step from `web/src/styles/rail-tokens.css`. The front page persuades; the app is worked in all day, so it keeps the world's palette, faces, square edges and stripes, and spends them on scanning speed rather than spectacle.
keyCharacteristics: Steel ground, paper objects, ink type; nothing else competes.
Age colours are state, never decoration.
Square corners everywhere; the only softness is the paper's own edge shadow.
Three faces, each tied to a speaker: the pass, the printer, the person.
State changes are instant; the one motion is the printer feeding the first ticket.

rules.name: The State-Only Rule
rules.body: The four age colours mean how long a lead has waited and nothing else. No link, heading, button, border or illustration uses them.

rules.name: The Stripe-Not-Text Rule
rules.body: Fresh Green, Heat-Lamp Orange and Late Red are stripes, never text or text grounds (Heat-Lamp Orange is 2.6:1 on paper). Every stripe has its label word beside it in ink, so colour is never the only signal.

rules.name: The Hottest-Colour Rule
rules.body: Only the lead that has waited longest gets its age word reversed out of Very Late Red. A claimed ticket's stripe turns to ink. In the app, where several leads can be very late at once, every Very late word is reversed: there it is a state, and the board sorts the longest wait first.

rules.name: The Three Speakers Rule
rules.body: Pick the face by who is speaking: the pass (Big Shoulders), the printer (Martian Mono), a person (Atkinson). Prose never runs in Big Shoulders, and printed output never runs in Atkinson.

rules.name: The Slashed Zero Rule
rules.body: Figures inside prose stay in the text face, slashed zero and all. Atkinson's zero is slashed for legibility and has no plain alternate; switching faces mid-sentence reads worse.

rules.name: The Paper-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: Only loose paper casts a shadow, and only the paper edge. Posted cards (the house card; in the app the sign-in card, a lead's card of keys, panels and notices) are framed in ink instead.

rules.name: The One Rule Rule
rules.body: When two pieces of paper are the same thing seen twice, a single 1px ink rule connects them. No arrows, no icons.

dos: **Do** put anything printed or written on paper and everything else directly on steel.
**Do** pair every age stripe with its word in ink: New, Waiting, Late, Very late.
**Do** change state instantly: a claimed ticket swaps its key for the stamp with no transition.
**Do** keep motion to the printer: the first ticket's printed fields feed in once on load (900ms, `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`, after 350ms), and only when the visitor allows motion.
**Do** label every figure built on made-up data as made-up, on the same line.
donts: **Don't** use an age colour for anything that is not a lead's waiting time.
**Don't** shadow anything that is not loose paper, and don't use any shadow but the paper edge.
**Don't** set prose in Big Shoulders or printed output in Atkinson.
**Don't** build the SaaS landing page: no headline beside a dashboard screenshot, no row of feature cards.
**Don't** use red for an error or a destructive key in the app; weight, the alert mark and the double frame carry it.
**Don't** read `ink` for text on steel in the app; read `on-steel`, or the night shift loses it.
